unmeasured: Not enough answers to place you here ({answered} of {expected} answered).
unsettled_note: You told us your views on several of these questions are still taking shape, but your answers lean clearly. Treat this result as where you stand today, not a fixed label.

matched.headline: Your closest perspective: {p1}
matched.subhead: Closest of the six perspectives we describe, not an exact match. You are also near {p2} and {p3}.

mixed_between.headline: You sit between {p1} and {p2}
mixed_between.body: Your answers fit two perspectives about equally well. Here is what you share with each, and the question that would tip you one way or the other.

mixed_unmatched.headline: Your own combination
mixed_unmatched.body: Your answers do not sit close to any of the six perspectives we describe. That usually means you combine views that are rarely held together, which is worth knowing. Here is what is distinctive about your profile. If you think we are missing a perspective, tell us.
mixed_unmatched.overlap: Your answers line up with {pairs}. None of the six captures your mix completely.
mixed_unmatched.nearest_label: Nearest of the six, though not close:
mixed_unmatched.missing_link: Think we're missing a perspective? Tell us

undecided.headline: Your views are still forming
undecided.body: You told us your views on several of these questions are still taking shape, and your answers do not lean strongly in one direction. That is a common place to be: in one 2025 Canadian poll, nearly a third of adults said they were not sure whether AI would be good or bad for society. Here is where you lean so far, and three questions worth thinking about.
undecided.coverage_body: You skipped enough questions that we cannot place you with confidence. Here is what we can say from the answers you gave.
undecided.lean_none: You're in between on all six questions so far.

indifferent.headline: AI is not high on your list
indifferent.body: You do not expect AI to change much for better or worse, and it is not among the issues you care most about. That is a legitimate position and a common one: in a large German study run over fifteen months, about half of adults named no AI concern at all. Here is how your views compare on the questions that divide people who do care.
indifferent.section_heading: Where you'd land if it came up
indifferent.section_body: Your six answers are on your full result. You're close to the middle on most of them, which is where a lot of people sit when AI isn't on their mind.

tensions.text: You expect AI to bring large benefits, and you still want more testing before powerful AI is widely released. You're willing to wait for gains you believe in.
You expect AI to bring both large benefits and serious harms. Many people hold both views at once; the question that matters for you is which arrives first.
You want new AI released quickly, and you want public regulators to have the final say on the rules. That combination works only if regulators can keep pace.
You want public oversight of AI, but you do not trust today's regulators to act in the public interest. Your position depends on oversight institutions that would have to be built or reformed.
You would leave rule-setting to industry and markets, though you do not trust AI companies to act in the public interest. You may be betting on competition rather than on the companies themselves.
You think AI will help a great deal, and you want humans to keep the final say on decisions about people. You are accepting some lost accuracy to keep accountability.
You want new AI released quickly and its gains shared widely. Speed and sharing usually come from different camps; you're asking for both.
You expect serious harms from AI and you still favour releasing it quickly. Perhaps you think holding back wouldn't prevent the harms, or that falling behind would be worse.
On the general questions you lean toward more testing before release, but when you had to choose, you picked earlier access with monitoring. Your view may depend on exactly what is being traded.
On the general questions you lean toward releasing AI sooner, but when you had to choose, you picked more testing first. Your view may depend on exactly what is being traded.

no_tension: Your answers pull in one direction more than most: {strongest_construct_name} is where you stand out most clearly.

statements.note: Pick the template by the direction of the shared or differing answer: _agree when the person agreed with the statement, _disagree when they disagreed. {short} is the item's short statement.
statements.unexpected_common_ground_agree: You and {perspective} are far apart overall, but you agree that {short}.
statements.unexpected_common_ground_disagree: You and {perspective} are far apart overall, but neither of you thinks {short}.
statements.friend_disagree_prompt: You split on whether {short}. Ask each other: what would change your mind?

why_this_result: Your result comes from your answers to {n_items} statements on six questions. For each question we averaged your answers (reversing the statements written from the other side), placed you on a scale from one side to the other, and found the perspective whose typical position is closest. The rules, the code and their known limits are published on the methodology page.
